scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 15 · KP05 The modified Hubert and Dunn indices

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Dunn index: closest inter-cluster distance over largest diameter, larger is better

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: the left is the source's hand example; the right is three-group data ($m=3$), where the dashed red line is the closest cross-cluster pair and the solid purple line the largest diameter.

scene-u01-pnew1-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew1-26.text: $d(C_i,C_j)$: closest pair across clusters; $\operatorname{diam}(C)$: farthest pair within a cluster

scene-u01-pnew1-128.name: text#128
scene-u01-pnew1-128.text: Source: if $D_m>1$, the clustering has compact, well-separated clusters

scene-u01-pnew1-129.name: text#129
scene-u01-pnew1-129.text: $D_m$ has no trend in $m$, so take its maximum

scene-u01-pnew1-130.name: text#130
scene-u01-pnew1-130.text: Source: week15-v01 lecture lec15-kp05-dunn-hubert §3 (hand example from the source)

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 15 · KP05 The modified Hubert and Dunn indices

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: One noise point can stretch a diameter: $D_3$ falls from $1.35$ below $1$

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: both panels show the same three-group data, the right with $6$ extra noise points (black rings); dashed red: closest cross-cluster pair, solid purple: largest diameter.

scene-u01-pnew2-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew2-8.text: Nearly the same clustering, yet the denominator grows and the numerator shrinks

scene-u01-pnew2-215.name: text#215
scene-u01-pnew2-215.text: Source: Dunn is costly and noise-sensitive—an outlier absorbed into a cluster stretches its diameter

scene-u01-pnew2-218.name: text#218
scene-u01-pnew2-218.text: Diameter $\operatorname{diam}^{\mathrm{MST}}$: largest edge of the cluster's MST

scene-u01-pnew2-219.name: text#219
scene-u01-pnew2-219.text: Inter-cluster distance: distance of the means $d(\mathbf{m}_i,\mathbf{m}_j)$

scene-u01-pnew2-220.name: text#220
scene-u01-pnew2-220.text: The largest MST edge measures the biggest gap, not the farthest pair

scene-u01-pnew2-227.name: text#227
scene-u01-pnew2-227.text: It drops with noise, but the maximum stays at $m=3$ and above $1$

scene-u01-pnew2-228.name: text#228
scene-u01-pnew2-228.text: Misconception: $D_m<1$ does not mean no structure ($D_m>1$ is one-way)

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 15 · KP05 The modified Hubert and Dunn indices

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Modified Hubert: find the knee; Dunn: take the maximum; both point to $m=3$

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: all three panels use $m=2,\dots,8$ across; green is three-group data, dashed gray uniform data, orange three-group data with noise; the thin dashed gray line marks $D=1$.

scene-u01-pnew3-9.name: text#9
scene-u01-pnew3-9.text: $Q(i,j)=d(\mathbf{w}_{c_i},\mathbf{w}_{c_j})$: distance between the two points' representatives

scene-u01-pnew3-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew3-41.text: Undefined at $m=1$ and $m=N$; more clusters bring $Q$ closer to $P$, so only a knee is informative

scene-u01-pnew3-75.name: text#75
scene-u01-pnew3-75.text: Green: three groups; orange: with $6$ noise points

scene-u01-pnew3-109.name: text#109
scene-u01-pnew3-109.text: Green: three groups; orange: with $6$ noise points

steps.label: The Dunn index
steps.speakerNotes: Closest inter-cluster distance over largest diameter; hand example D2=3; three-group data at m=3 give D3=2.52/1.87=1.35>1.

steps.label: Noise and the MST version
steps.speakerNotes: With 6 noise points the largest diameter is 3.02 and the closest pair 2.18, so D3 falls to 0.72; the MST version drops from 6.85 to 2.65, still above 1.

steps.label: Three indices against m
steps.speakerNotes: Modified Hubert jumps to 0.966 at m=3 then flattens, while uniform data keep rising; Dunn and the MST version peak at m=3.
